column2: req_desc

Studio accounts and sign-in
A studio entrant creates a studio account or signs in with email and password, and every seeded director, juror and studio can sign in, with the session held in an HttpOnly cookie as set out in API.

One error order for every endpoint
Every protected endpoint answers by the single error-precedence rule and error shapes in API, and unauthenticated calls to protected endpoints answer 401.

Programs and categories
The program director creates programs with a time zone, early-bird and entry deadline dates and two fees, edits those dates, and adds categories with a shortlist size and finalist count, all validated as stated in API.

Deadlines in the program's time zone
Entry, early-bird and withdrawal-refund cutoffs are judged on the server against the end of 23:59 in the program's time zone, and every deadline an entrant sees, on screen or in email, carries the label format from Business rules regardless of the browser's zone.

Entry drafts
A studio entrant creates, edits and deletes draft entries in an open category, and deleting a draft removes its case-study images from storage.

Case-study image checks
Uploads are judged by their content, size and pixel dimensions with the limits, order and rejections in Business rules, and an accepted image is stored with its detected type, width, height and byte size.

Re-encoded images served back
Only server re-encoded image bytes are ever served, from storage keys the server chooses, to callers allowed to see the entry.

Fee in effect at payment time
The fee charged is the early-bird fee while the early-bird window is open at the moment of payment and the standard fee afterwards, and the receipt, Kill Bill invoice and screen all show that tier.

All-or-nothing submission
An entry becomes submitted only when its fee is paid in Kill Bill, its images are in storage and its receipt email is sent; any failure leaves an unpaid draft with no successful charge, as qualified in Business rules.

One payment per idempotency key
Repeating a submission with the same idempotency key returns the stored response with exactly one invoice, one payment and one receipt, and reusing the key for a different entry answers 409.

Billing outage keeps the draft
When Kill Bill is unreachable the desk still starts, answers payment and refund attempts with the payments-paused 503, keeps the draft or entry unchanged, and accepts the payment on the next attempt once billing answers, with no restart.

Studio records stay private
A studio reaches only its own entries, receipts, invoices and draft images, and any other studio's id answers 404.

Withdrawal and refund
A studio withdraws a submitted entry before the deadline with a full Kill Bill refund and a refund email, or after the deadline with no refund, and every other withdrawal answers 409, as qualified in Business rules.

Screening and reinstatement
After the deadline the director passes or disqualifies submitted entries with a reason and may reinstate a disqualified entry, and the studio sees the status and reason.

Director-only actions
Creating programs, categories and jurors, screening, reinstating, adding jurors to a panel, opening, closing and confirming rounds and publishing results are refused with 403 for jurors and studios.

Juror accounts and declared conflicts
The director creates juror accounts with an optional home studio, and a juror declares conflicts with named studios, which immediately removes those studios' entries from every open or scheduled round the juror sits on.

Conflict-free assignment
A juror on a round panel is assigned every entry in the round except entries from the juror's home studio or a declared-conflict studio.

Recusal mid-round
A juror recusing from an entry in an open round loses that assignment and any score for it is excluded from the round result.

Round state machine
Rounds move scheduled, open, closed, normalised, published only by director action with the guards in Business rules, and every illegal step answers 409.

Blind ballot
A juror's ballot and the jury packet carry each entry's number, title, case-study text and images only, never studio name, email, credits or site address.

Scoring and final ballot
A juror scores Craft, Clarity, Idea and Story from 1 to 10 for each assigned entry, sees how many remain, and submits a final ballot only when every assignment is scored, after which scores are locked.

Ballot against round close
A final ballot submitted while the director closes the round either counts in the stored result with 200 or is refused with the round-closed 409, never both or partly.

Normalised round score
Closing a round computes and stores each entry's score once by the weighting, per-juror normalisation, trimming and rounding in Business rules.

Ranking and the cut
Standings rank by score, then higher Idea mean, then earlier submission, and mark each row above or below the category's cut, with provisional standings while a round is open.

Confirming standings
Confirming a closed round turns its standings into shortlisted and eliminated entries in Round 1, or winner, finalist and honourable mention in the final round.

Embargoed publishing
Publishing a category with an embargo time keeps every result off public surfaces and studio-facing results until that time passes, as qualified in Business rules.

Results notice email
When a category's embargo passes each entering studio gets one results email carrying only its own entries' outcomes and rounded scores, never juror names, per-juror scores or other studios' details, as qualified in Business rules.

Public gallery and leaderboard
The public gallery and leaderboard return only the published field list for revealed entries, filterable by year, category and award level.

Counts agree with rows
Per-category state counts, per-juror ballots remaining and leaderboard ranks always equal what the stored entries, assignments and scores imply.

Director audit trail
Every successful director action writes exactly one audit event the director can list, newest first.

Jury packet and invitations
Opening a round stores a blind jury packet in storage and emails each panel juror an invitation with the ballot deadline and assignment count, as qualified in Business rules.

Entrant journey
A studio entrant signs in, drafts an entry, adds images, pays, gets one receipt and sees the entry as submitted with its receipt in the browser.

Juror journey
A juror signs in, opens the round ballot, scores every blind entry, submits the final ballot and sees it confirmed in the browser.

Director judging journey
The director screens entries, builds a panel, opens and closes a round, watches the standings and confirms the shortlist in the browser.

Public reveal journey
A public visitor opens the leaderboard, watches a category revealed at its embargo time and finds the winners in the gallery.

The Cut Shuffle
When standings change, each affected row rolls its score, travels to its new rank, swaps its cut marker as it crosses the cut and a summary is announced last, with the timings in Motion and effects.

Reduced-motion standings
With reduced motion requested, standings re-order instantly with static up or down delta labels and the same announcement, and no other element animates.

Status by glyph and label
Above-cut, below-cut, winner, finalist and honourable-mention status always shows a glyph and a text label, never colour alone, and text meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast.

Responsive layout
Every screen works at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 with no horizontal overflow and tap targets at least 44 pixels.

Keyboard and focus
Every control is reachable by Tab in visual order with a visible focus ring, dialogs trap focus, Escape closes them and focus returns to the control that opened them.

Visual identity
Screens use the paper, ink, signal, cut and rule colour roles, the extra-wide display face for category headers, the body face and monospaced two-decimal scores described in Visual design.

Ranked-table composition
Standings, leaderboard and entry lists sit on a visible twelve-column hairline grid as full-width ranked tables under a sticky black band with the round name and countdown.

Health, manifest and boundary
The app starts from /app/run.json on the configured port, answers the health check, and the server boundary rules on origin, body size and never-served files hold.

Credentials from the environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment named in Configuration and secrets and never appears in source or browser-delivered code.

Real provider effects
Payments, refunds, images, packets and emails are real Kill Bill, storage and Mailpit operations, and no state the brief assigns to a provider is kept only in the app.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve commands and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and those commands alone install, build and serve the app.

/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md names every shipped package and its licence, plus each bundled font and icon set; shipped packages means the production dependency tree reported by npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.
Every shipped package, font and icon set is licensed under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, BlueOak-1.0.0, CC0-1.0 or SIL OFL-1.1.
The app stores state only in the provided Postgres, Kill Bill, MinIO and Mailpit services; no SQLite, Redis, embedded database or state kept in local files.
The provided service configuration, compose files and environment variable names are left unchanged.
Application source is TypeScript; JavaScript appears only as generated build output or tool configuration.
